comments.author: @UnrealWorldJourney1
comments.text: Scotland becomes even more impressive once you leave the famous landmarks behind. 🏔 The isolated glens, windswept islands and remote Highland communities reveal how strongly geography has shaped Scottish history and identity. In places like Glencoe, Skye and the Outer Hebrides, the landscape doesn’t just provide scenery, it explains why communities developed so differently from those in the cities.

replies.author: @Earthcue
replies.text: Absolutely! Scotland’s landscapes really do tell a story, especially once you get beyond the well known sights. The connection between geography, history, and local communities is fascinating.
